questions.q:
Consider the following statements about legislation passed by Parliament in April 2026:
1. The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026, which decriminalises minor offences in central Acts, was cleared by the Rajya Sabha on 2 April 2026 after the Lok Sabha had passed it.
2. The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026 amended Section 5(2) of the 2014 Act to make Amaravati the sole and permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh.
3. Under the original Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was to be the common capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for a period of up to fifteen years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Both Bills cleared the Rajya Sabha on 2 April 2026: Jan Vishwas rationalises minor offences (an earlier 2023 Act did the same for 42 Acts), and the AP Bill gave statutory backing to the Assembly's resolution on Amaravati. The 2014 Act allowed Hyderabad to serve as common capital for up to ten years, a period that ended in June 2024, so statement 3 inflates the period.
questions.s: All India Radio and PRS India, 2 Apr 2026

questions.q: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, aimed at speeding up one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, was defeated in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026 by 298 votes to 230. Which one of the following best explains the defeat, although more members voted for the Bill than against it?
o: A constitutional amendment Bill needs only a simple majority of members present and voting, and the Bill failed to reach it
A constitutional amendment Bill must have the prior ratification of at least half of the State legislatures before it can be put to vote in the Lok Sabha
A constitutional amendment Bill needs a three-fourths majority of the total membership of the House
A constitutional amendment Bill needs, in addition to a majority of the total membership of the House, a two-thirds majority of members present and voting, which 298 of 528 votes did not meet
questions.e: Article 368 requires a majority of the total membership of the House and not less than two-thirds of members present and voting. With 528 members voting, two-thirds was 352, so 298 votes fell well short even though they outnumbered the 230 against. State ratification (for federal subjects) comes only after both Houses pass the Bill, and the three-fourths figure applies to State ratification, not the Lok Sabha vote.
questions.s: PRS India and Moneylife, 17 Apr 2026
questions.h: Two tests: Total majority + two-thirds present

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Opposition notices seeking the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner, which were in the news in April 2026:
1. The Rajya Sabha Chairman and the Lok Sabha Speaker refused to admit the notices on 6 April 2026, the first time such notices had been moved in both Houses together.
2. Under the proviso to Article 324(5), the Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
3. Under Article 324(5), the other Election Commissioners can be removed by the President on his own, without any recommendation from the Chief Election Commissioner.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The presiding officers cited the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 and held that no prima facie misbehaviour was made out. The CEC enjoys judge-like security of tenure under the proviso to Article 324(5), which is why a removal motion follows the Judges (Inquiry) Act route. The other Election Commissioners are weaker: they can be removed only on the recommendation of the CEC, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: All India Radio, Business Today and Onmanorama, 6 Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the merger of seven Aam Aadmi Party Rajya Sabha members with the BJP, accepted by the Rajya Sabha Chairman on 27 April 2026:
1. The merger was accepted under paragraph 4 of the Tenth Schedule, which protects members from disqualification if not less than two-thirds of the legislature party agree to the merger.
2. The 91st Constitutional Amendment (2003) removed the earlier exception that had protected a split of one-third of the members of a legislature party.
3. A petition for disqualification of a Rajya Sabha member under the Tenth Schedule is decided by the President after consulting the Election Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Seven of ten AAP members is 70 per cent, above the two-thirds mark in paragraph 4, which is why the Chairman treated it as a protected merger (AAP argued that the original party must itself merge). The 91st Amendment scrapped the one-third 'split' protection to curb mass defections. Under paragraph 6, disqualification is decided by the presiding officer, here the Rajya Sabha Chairman, not the President.
questions.s: Tribune and India TV, 27 Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Assembly elections held in April 2026:
1. Tamil Nadu voted on 9 April 2026 together with Kerala, Assam and Puducherry.
2. Counting of votes for all the five States/Union Territories that went to the polls took place together on 4 May 2026.
3. West Bengal voted in two phases, on 23 April and 29 April 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Kerala, Assam and Puducherry voted in a single phase on 9 April, Tamil Nadu on 23 April, and West Bengal in two phases (23 and 29 April), with a common counting day on 4 May. Statement 1 wrongly groups Tamil Nadu with the 9 April States.
questions.s: Sakshi Post and WION, 15 Mar and 9 Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Supreme Court judgments of April 2026:
1. In Sathyan Naravoor v. Union of India, the Court held that the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 applies fully in custodial settings such as prisons.
2. In the Phalodi Accident case, the Court held that commuter safety on roads is part of the right to life with dignity under Article 21 and issued interim directions under Article 142.
3. In Sathyan Naravoor, the Court held that incarceration dilutes the guarantees of dignity and equality under Articles 14 and 21 to the extent required by prison administration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court extended the framework for prisoners with disabilities to all States and UTs and held the opposite of statement 3: incarceration does not dilute the dignity and equality guarantees. In the Phalodi case, taken up suo motu after 34 road deaths, it barred heavy vehicles from parking on National Highway carriageways and ordered District Highway Safety Task Forces.
questions.s: SC Observer and Verdictum, Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sathankulam custodial deaths case:
1. In April 2026 a Madurai court sentenced nine police personnel to death for the custodial deaths of P. Jayaraj and his son Bennix, in a case tried on a CBI chargesheet.
2. A death sentence passed by a Sessions Court can be carried out without confirmation by the High Court.
3. The father and son were detained in June 2020 in Sathankulam in Thoothukudi district, and the accused were convicted in March 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Madurai court sentenced all nine convicted police personnel to death on 6 April 2026 after convicting them on 23 March. Statement 2 is wrong because a death sentence from a Sessions Court has to be confirmed by the High Court before it can be executed, which is a standard safeguard in capital cases.
questions.s: LiveLaw and IANS, 6 Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Online Gaming Authority of India, constituted by the Union government in April 2026, is an attached office of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and is chaired by an Additional Secretary of that Ministry.
2. The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026 came into force on 1 May 2026 under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025.
3. In State of Tamil Nadu v. Junglee Games India Pvt. Ltd. (2026), the Supreme Court held that betting on games of skill enjoys protection under Article 19(1)(g).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Authority has six members, and the Rules operationalise the 2025 Act, which bars online money games. In Junglee Games the Court upheld the Tamil Nadu and Karnataka laws, holding that betting on games of skill is not protected as a trade under Article 19(1)(g), and relied on Entry 34 (betting and gambling) of the State List.
questions.s: India TV News, LiveLaw and Verdictum, Apr-May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026:
1. It raised the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court from 34 to 38, including the Chief Justice of India.
2. It amends the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956.
3. Under Article 124(1), the number of Supreme Court Judges can be increased only through a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The President promulgated the Ordinance on 16 May 2026 under Article 123. Article 124(1) fixes the number only 'until Parliament by law prescribes a larger number', so an ordinary law (here the 1956 Act, as amended) suffices and no Article 368 amendment is needed. An ordinance must be laid before Parliament and lapses six weeks after it reassembles unless approved earlier.
questions.s: All India Radio and SCC Online, 16 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On 27 May 2026 the Supreme Court held that the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of Bihar's electoral rolls derives from Article 326 alone and overrides the provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
2. In Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India (2023), a Constitution Bench placed the Chief Justice of India on the panel selecting Election Commissioners until Parliament made a law.
3. Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, the selection committee comprises the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court held that SIR flows from Article 324 read with Section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and does not override existing election law, so statement 1 is wrong. The 2023 Act dropped the CJI that Anoop Baranwal had placed on the panel, and challenges to it were heard by a Division Bench from 6 May 2026.
questions.s: Business Today, SC Observer and Superkalam, May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs about State politics in April-May 2026 (State : Development):
1. Tamil Nadu : Vijay's TVK emerged as the largest party with 108 of 234 seats, short of the majority mark of 118
2. West Bengal : BJP won 207 of 294 seats and Suvendu Adhikari became the first BJP Chief Minister of the State
3. Kerala : LDF retained power by winning 102 of 140 seats
4. Bihar : Samrat Choudhary became the first BJP Chief Minister of the State after Nitish Kumar was elected to the Rajya Sabha
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 3 is wrong: in Kerala the Congress-led UDF won 102 of 140 seats and V.D. Satheesan took oath on 18 May, ending a decade of LDF rule. In Tamil Nadu the hung House (majority mark 118) saw C. Joseph Vijay win a floor test with support from some parties of the DMK-led alliance, and in Bihar Samrat Choudhary was sworn in on 15 April after Nitish Kumar resigned.
questions.s: Scroll, The Statesman, WION and Business Today, Apr-May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sabarimala reference:
1. The Supreme Court's nine-judge Constitution Bench reserved its verdict on 14 May 2026.
2. The reference was made in November 2018 by the bench that decided Indian Young Lawyers Association v. State of Kerala.
3. The reference examines the interplay of Articles 25, 26 and 14 and the extent of judicial interference in religious practices.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The reference was made in November 2019, when a five-judge bench was hearing review petitions against the 2018 judgment that allowed women of all ages into the temple, not in 2018 itself. Hearings before the nine-judge bench began on 7 April 2026 and the verdict was reserved on 14 May.
questions.s: UNI and Verdictum, 14 May 2026

questions.q:
Statement-I: On 15 May 2026 the Madhya Pradesh High Court held that the Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act, 1991 does not apply to the Bhojshala-Kamal Maula complex in Dhar.
Statement-II: Section 4(3) of the 1991 Act exempts ancient monuments and archaeological sites protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The complex is a protected monument, and Section 4(3) of the 1991 Act carves out such monuments from its bar on converting or contesting the religious character of places of worship as they stood on 15 August 1947. That exemption is the reason the Court could hear the writ petition under Article 226 and declare the complex a temple of Goddess Vagdevi.
questions.s: Deccan Herald and The Wire, 15 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In 2022, in S.G. Vombatkere v. Union of India, the Supreme Court kept Section 124A IPC (sedition) in abeyance and barred fresh FIRs under it.
2. In May 2026, the Supreme Court allowed trial courts to continue trials and appeals under Section 124A where the accused does not object.
3. Section 152 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 retains the word 'sedition' and re-enacts Section 124A in its original form.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Section 124A has been in abeyance since the 2022 order, and in Kamran v. State of Madhya Pradesh the Court relaxed this for willing accused. The BNS dropped the word 'sedition': Section 152 instead penalises acts endangering the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India, so it is not a re-enactment in the original form.
questions.s: Drishti IAS and ETV Bharat, 21 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, popularly called VB-G RAM G:
1. It will operate alongside the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, which stays in force for States that opt out of the new Act.
2. It guarantees 125 days of wage employment per rural household in a financial year, against 100 days under the MGNREGA.
3. Wages under the Act are payable within 15 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act came into force on 1 July 2026 in all States and UTs and repealed the MGNREGA the same day, so statement 1 is wrong. It is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development, with Centre-State funding of 60:40 for most States and 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.
questions.s: Business Standard and All India Radio, May-Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's order of 19 May 2026 on stray dogs:
1. The Court refused to recall its November 2025 directions that stray dogs picked up from public places must not be released back after sterilisation or vaccination.
2. It allowed States to euthanise rabid or demonstrably dangerous dogs through legally permissible procedures.
3. It asked the Animal Welfare Board of India, instead of the High Courts, to monitor compliance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court directed States and Union Territories to set up Animal Birth Control centres, ensure anti-rabies vaccine availability and confine such dogs to shelters, and asked High Courts to monitor compliance through suo motu cases. The statutory framework for sterilisation and vaccination is the Animal Birth Control (Dogs) Rules, 2023.
questions.s: All India Radio, 19 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the proposed amendment cleared by the Union Cabinet in May 2026 relating to the national song Vande Mataram:
1. The proposal amends the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 so that insulting Vande Mataram attracts penalties similar to those for insulting the National Anthem.
2. Section 3 of the 1971 Act provides for imprisonment up to three years, a fine, or both, for intentionally preventing the singing of the National Anthem.
3. Vande Mataram was first published in Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's novel Durgeshnandini.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Section 3 of the 1971 Act punishes preventing the singing of the National Anthem or disturbing an assembly engaged in singing it. Vande Mataram appeared in Bankim Chandra's novel Anandamath, not Durgeshnandini.
questions.s: Drishti IAS and The Statesman, May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's judgment in Maniyar Iliyaz v. P. Ayyappan (June 2026):
1. The Court held that the right to walk on safe, demarcated footpaths is a fundamental right flowing from Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(d).
2. The Court held that the duty to build and maintain footpaths lies only on State Governments and not on municipal bodies or panchayats.
3. The Court directed its Registry to forward the judgment to the Law Commission of India and the concerned Union Ministries to initiate a legal framework.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court held that urban development authorities, municipal bodies and panchayats all have an enforceable duty to demarcate, build and maintain footpaths, and that pedestrians' right to designated footpaths takes precedence over motorised vehicles. It also urged dedicated pedestrian-rights legislation.
questions.s: Drishti IAS and Moneylife, Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Delhi High Court held in June 2026 that the right to be forgotten forms part of the right to privacy under Article 21, though not an absolute right.
2. India has a standalone statute that expressly recognises the right to be forgotten.
3. In Seesa Santosh v. State of Telangana (2026), the Supreme Court held that the right to travel abroad, part of personal liberty under Article 21, is not absolute and must be balanced against the complainant's right to a speedy trial.
4. In Shishu Pal v. Surjeet (2026), the Supreme Court created a separate head of 'loss of domestic care' in motor accident claims on the death of a homemaker.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. There is no standalone statute on the right to be forgotten in India; it is derived from privacy as a fundamental right recognised in K.S. Puttaswamy (2017). In Shishu Pal the Court added a composite Rs 30,000 per month for loss of domestic care, rising by 10 per cent every three years.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, Deccan Herald and SC Observer, Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Rules, 2026 notified by the Ministry of Home Affairs:
1. They introduce activity-specific and State/UT-specific registration with separate fees.
2. NGOs must use at least 75 per cent of previous funds before receiving further instalments.
3. Foreign funds may be used for proselytisation provided the activity is disclosed to the Ministry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rules also require disclosure of the ultimate donor and social media accounts. They permit foreign funds for worship, religious education, heritage preservation and community kitchens, but not for proselytisation, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Drishti IAS and PRS India, Jun 2026

questions.q: With reference to Census 2027, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Phase I (houselisting) runs from 1 April to 30 September 2026, and caste enumeration forms part of Phase II (population enumeration) planned for February 2027
Caste enumeration is part of Phase I, the houselisting operation running from 1 April to 30 September 2026
The reference date for population enumeration is 1 March 2027 in every part of the country, including Ladakh
Phase II (population enumeration) begins in April 2026 alongside Phase I
questions.e: Each State/UT gets a 15-day online self-enumeration window followed by a 30-day door-to-door field operation in Phase I. The reference date is 1 March 2027 for most areas but 1 October 2026 for Ladakh and snow-bound non-synchronous areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
questions.s: All India Radio, Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha elections of June 2026:
1. Rajya Sabha members from a State are elected by the elected members of its Legislative Assembly through proportional representation by the single transferable vote.
2. In Madhya Pradesh the nomination of Congress candidate Meenakshi Natarajan was rejected at scrutiny on 9 June 2026, after which the BJP's three candidates were elected unopposed.
3. Under Article 329(b), a rejected nomination can be challenged in court immediately during the election process, without waiting for an election petition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Returning Officer acted on a BJP objection that she had not disclosed a pending case. Article 329(b) bars courts from interfering in an election in progress and channels disputes to an election petition after the result, so statement 3 is wrong. The poll was for 24 seats in 10 States, with notification on 1 June and polling on 18 June.
questions.s: India TV News, Scroll and All India Radio, Jun 2026

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the 11th Governing Council meeting of NITI Aayog, held on 11 June 2026, is NOT correct?
o: The meeting was chaired by the Prime Minister on the theme 'Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047'
A target of raising the number of Lakhpati Didis from 3 crore to 6 crore was highlighted
NITI Aayog was established in 2015 and replaced the Planning Commission
NITI Aayog is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament, which is why its Governing Council could be convened
questions.e: NITI Aayog was set up by an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet on 1 January 2015 and is neither a constitutional nor a statutory body. Its Governing Council includes Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories, and the meeting also urged States to prepare district-level GDP estimates.
questions.s: Drishti IAS and Onmanorama, 11 Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the temporary blocking of the Telegram messaging app in June 2026:
1. The Centre blocked the app under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
2. The order was linked to the National Testing Agency's recommendation to prevent paper-leak rackets ahead of the NEET (UG) 2026 re-examination of 21 June.
3. The blocking order was issued by the National Testing Agency under its own statutory powers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The notification came from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology under the 2009 Blocking Rules framed under Section 69A, not from the NTA, which only recommended it. NEET-UG 2026 held in May had been cancelled over a paper leak, hence the re-examination.
questions.s: ETV Bharat, The News Minute and The South First, 16 Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the tripartite MoU signed on 11 June 2026 by the Government of India, Assam and Nagaland:
1. It enables mineral oil exploration and production in sectors along the disputed Assam-Nagaland boundary.
2. Fees, royalties and taxes from such operations are shared between the two States in a 60:40 ratio in favour of Assam.
3. It settles the boundary dispute and ends the Original Suit filed by Assam in the Supreme Court in 1988.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Revenues are shared 50:50, and the arrangement is an interim one, expressly without prejudice to either State's territorial claims, so Assam's Original Suit No. 2 of 1988 continues in the Supreme Court. Disputes go to an Empowered Committee of Secretaries and then an Empowered Group of Ministers.
questions.s: India TV News, Morung Express and Swarajya, 11 Jun 2026
